quote.text: Where has the horse gone? Where the rider? Where the giver of treasure?

levelNote: The main facts, names and dates of the age.

questions.question: Which three Germanic tribes migrated to Britain around 449 AD as recorded by Bede?
questions.explanation: Bede records that three main Germanic tribes migrated around 449 AD: Angles, Saxons, and Jutes.

questions.question: Who were the legendary twin brothers who led the Germanic migration to Britain around 449 AD?
questions.explanation: Hengist and Horsa were the legendary twin brothers invited by Vortigern around 449 AD.

questions.question: Which British warlord invited Hengist and Horsa to defend against Pictish incursions?
questions.explanation: The British warlord Vortigern invited Hengist and Horsa before they turned against him.

questions.question: In which year did St. Augustine arrive in Kent on the Roman Mission sent by Pope Gregory I?
questions.explanation: Pope Gregory I dispatched St. Augustine to Kent in 597 AD to establish the see at Canterbury.

questions.question: Where did St. Augustine establish the first archbishopric see in England in 597 AD?
questions.explanation: St. Augustine established the see at Canterbury after arriving at the court of King Aethelberht.

questions.question: Who founded the Celtic monastic settlement at Iona in 563 AD?
questions.explanation: Irish monasticism expanded from Iona, which was founded by St. Columba in 563 AD.

questions.question: Which Celtic monk established the monastery of Lindisfarne in Northumbria in 635 AD?
questions.explanation: St. Aidan established the monastery of Lindisfarne in 635 AD under Northumbrian King Oswald.

questions.question: Which ecclesiastical synod in 664 AD aligned the English Church with Roman usages?
questions.explanation: The Synod of Whitby in 664 AD resolved liturgical friction and adopted Roman usages.

questions.question: Which Northumbrian king convened the Synod of Whitby in 664 AD?
questions.explanation: The Synod of Whitby was convened in 664 AD by King Oswiu of Northumbria.

questions.question: In which year did the historic Viking raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne take place?
questions.explanation: The Viking raid on Lindisfarne in 793 AD marked the beginning of Scandinavian incursions.

questions.question: During which historical years did King Alfred the Great reign over Wessex?
questions.explanation: King Alfred the Great reigned over Wessex from 871 to 899 AD.

questions.question: In which year did the Battle of Maldon take place?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Maldon took place in 991 AD when English forces met Viking raiders.

questions.question: Which decisive event in 1066 ended the Anglo-Saxon political era?
questions.explanation: The Norman Conquest under William I in 1066 marked the end of the Anglo-Saxon era.

questions.question: How many distinct regional dialects of Old English developed across Anglo-Saxon Britain?
questions.explanation: Old English developed across four distinct regional dialects: Northumbrian, Mercian, Kentish, and West Saxon.

questions.question: Which Old English dialect became the standardized literary language known as Schriftsprache?
questions.explanation: Late West Saxon became the standardized literary language of Anglo-Saxon scribes.

questions.question: What is the structural term for the pause dividing an Old English alliterative line into two half-lines?
questions.explanation: A medial caesura is the distinct structural pause separating the two hemistichs.

questions.question: How many strongly stressed syllables are present in a full Old English alliterative line?
questions.explanation: Every full line contains four strongly stressed syllables, two in each half-line.

questions.question: What is the first stressed syllable of the b-verse called in Old English alliterative verse?
questions.explanation: The first stressed syllable of the b-verse is the head-stave, which must alliterate with the a-verse.

questions.question: Who categorized Old English half-lines into five metrical types labeled A through E?
questions.explanation: Eduard Sievers categorized Old English half-lines into five metrical patterns, Types A through E.

questions.question: What is the figurative Old English compound noun 'hwoel-rad' or 'whale-road' an example of?
questions.explanation: A kenning is a specialized metaphorical compound noun describing an object or concept.

questions.question: What does the Old English kenning 'ban-hus' or 'bone-house' signify?
questions.explanation: Ban-hus translates to bone-house, which is the kenning for the human body.

questions.question: What does the Old English kenning 'gomen-wudu' or 'mirth-wood' mean?
questions.explanation: Gomen-wudu translates to mirth-wood, a kenning for the harp.

questions.question: What does the Old English kenning 'beado-leoma' or 'battle-light' refer to?
questions.explanation: Beado-leoma translates to battle-light, a kenning for a sword.

questions.question: Which rhetorical device describes grim, ironic understatement in Old English poetry?
questions.explanation: Litotes is a form of ironic understatement used for grim or heroic effect.

questions.question: Which scholars formulated the oral-formulaic theory applied to Old English poetry by Francis P. Magoun?
questions.explanation: Oral-formulaic theory was formulated by Milman Parry and Albert Lord.

questions.question: Which manuscript holds the unique surviving text of the epic poem 'Beowulf'?
questions.explanation: The Nowell Codex, Cotton Vitellius A. xv, preserves the sole surviving copy of Beowulf.

questions.question: What is the modern library shelfmark of the Nowell Codex in the British Library?
questions.explanation: The Nowell Codex is cataloged as Cotton Vitellius A. xv in the British Library.

questions.question: Which cathedral library houses the tenth-century Exeter Book of Old English poetry?
questions.explanation: The Exeter Book has been preserved in Exeter Cathedral Library since Bishop Leofric donated it.

questions.question: Which eleventh-century bishop donated the Exeter Book to Exeter Cathedral around 1072?
questions.explanation: Bishop Leofric donated the codex around 1072, describing it as a large English book in verse.

questions.question: In which country is the tenth-century Vercelli Book preserved today?
questions.explanation: The Vercelli Book is preserved in the cathedral library of Vercelli in northern Italy.

questions.question: Which of the four major Old English poetic manuscripts features visual line illustrations?
questions.explanation: The Junius Manuscript is unique among the four for featuring visual line illustrations.

questions.question: What is the total line count of the Old English epic 'Beowulf'?
questions.explanation: Beowulf is an epic poem of exactly 3,182 lines preserved in the Nowell Codex.

questions.question: What is the name of King Hrothgar's grand mead-hall cleansed by Beowulf?
questions.explanation: King Hrothgar's royal mead-hall in Denmark is named Heorot.

questions.question: Which monstrous creature terrorizes Heorot at the opening of 'Beowulf'?
questions.explanation: Grendel terrorizes Heorot for twelve winters before Beowulf defeats him.

questions.question: Who is the only loyal retainer who stays to help Beowulf fight the dragon?
questions.explanation: Wiglaf alone among Beowulf's retainers remains loyal and aids him against the dragon.

questions.question: What Old English term designates the inexorable force of fate governing mortal life?
questions.explanation: Wyrd is the Old English term for fate, the force governing human destiny.

questions.question: Which heroic concept describes the reciprocal bond of absolute loyalty between a lord and his retainers?
questions.explanation: The comitatus code defines the mutual loyalty and ring-giving bond between lord and retainers.

questions.question: Who was the English commander killed at the Battle of Maldon in 991 AD?
questions.explanation: Earl Byrhtnoth led the Anglo-Saxon defenders and fell in combat at Maldon.

questions.question: Which Old English term in 'The Battle of Maldon' describes Byrhtnoth's tragic over-confidence or excessive pride?
questions.explanation: Byrhtnoth yielded ground across the causeway because of ofermod, over-confidence or pride.

questions.question: Which English king won the historic Battle of Brunanburh in 937 AD alongside his brother Edmund?
questions.explanation: King Athelstan of Wessex and his brother Edmund defeated the northern alliance at Brunanburh.

questions.question: In which historical chronicle is the poem 'The Battle of Brunanburh' preserved under the year 937 AD?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Brunanburh is preserved as the annal entry for 937 AD in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

questions.question: Which Old English poem presents a catalog of heroic tribes and rulers through the persona of a wandering scop?
questions.explanation: Widsith, meaning Far-Traveler, catalogs the ancient Germanic rulers, heroes, and tribes.

questions.question: What is the persona of the speaker in the Old English elegy 'The Wanderer'?
questions.explanation: The Wanderer is spoken by an isolated exile described as an earth-treader, an eardstapa.

questions.question: Which famous Latin rhetorical motif asking 'Where are they now?' features prominently in 'The Wanderer'?
questions.explanation: The Wanderer includes a famous passage of the Ubi sunt motif beginning Hwær cwom mearg.

questions.question: What is the recurring Old English refrain in the elegy 'Deor'?
options: Hwær cwom mearg, hwær cwom mago
questions.explanation: Deor repeats the strophic refrain Thæs ofereode, thisses swa mæg, meaning That passed over, so may this.

questions.question: Which ancient Roman city ruins in Britain are generally identified as the subject of 'The Ruin'?
questions.explanation: Scholars generally identify the decayed stone baths and walls in The Ruin as Aquae Sulis, modern Bath.

questions.question: Who was the illiterate herdsman at Whitby Abbey who miraculously received the gift of poetic song?
questions.explanation: Caedmon was the cowherd at Whitby Abbey who received the divine gift of song as recorded by Bede.

questions.question: How many lines comprise 'Caedmon's Hymn', the oldest surviving text of Old English poetry?
questions.explanation: Caedmon's Hymn is a nine-line devotional lyric praising God as the Creator of the cosmos.

questions.question: How did the poet Cynewulf sign his name in the epilogues of his four signed poems?
options: With a dedication to King Alfred
With runic letters woven as an acrostic
questions.explanation: Cynewulf wove his name in runic characters C-Y-N-E-W-U-L-F into the epilogues of his works.

questions.question: Lines from which Old English religious dream vision are carved in runes on the eighth-century Ruthwell Cross?
questions.explanation: Passages from The Dream of the Rood are inscribed in runic letters on the Ruthwell Cross in Scotland.
